inputs.name: packages
inputs.description: Extra Cockpit pages to install, such as ["cockpit-podman", "cockpit-machines"].

inputs.name: backports
inputs.description: On Debian and Ubuntu, install Cockpit from the release's backports, as Cockpit's own install guide does. On Debian, the circuit adds the backports repository when it's missing.

inputs.name: address
inputs.description: IP address Cockpit listens on, such as "127.0.0.1" behind a reverse proxy. When null, every address.

inputs.name: origins
inputs.description: Other origins the browser may reach Cockpit from, such as ["https://cockpit.example.com"] behind a reverse proxy. Cockpit always accepts its own address.

inputs.name: login_title
inputs.description: Browser title for the login page. When null, Cockpit's default, the host name.

inputs.name: allow_unencrypted
inputs.description: Accept plain HTTP from other hosts instead of redirecting it to HTTPS. Only for a reverse proxy that talks HTTP to Cockpit; Cockpit always accepts HTTP from localhost.

inputs.name: behind_proxy
inputs.description: Trust the X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-For headers from a reverse proxy. Set it only when nothing but the proxy can reach Cockpit's port.

inputs.name: tls_certificate
inputs.description: Path on the host of a PEM certificate, with its chain, for Cockpit to serve, such as "/etc/letsencrypt/live/cockpit.example.com/fullchain.pem". When null, Cockpit's self-signed certificate.

inputs.name: tls_key
inputs.description: Path on the host of the unencrypted private key for tls_certificate, such as "/etc/letsencrypt/live/cockpit.example.com/privkey.pem".

inputs.name: root_login
inputs.description: Let root log in to Cockpit with its password. When false, root is in /etc/cockpit/disallowed-users; log in as an administrator and switch to administrative access instead.
